page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.32-512 is an enterprise virtual machine instance configured within the flexible Standard E6 family. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. It provides 32 dedicated physical cores supporting multithreading with two threads per core, delivering 64 vCPUs to the guest operating system without hypervisor resource contention.

The hardware configuration includes 512 GB of system RAM, maintaining a density of 8 GB per vCPU. This memory ratio situates the server in a memory-optimized operational profile. The instance bundles no local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent file systems and runtime data storage rely on external network-attached block volumes. It features zero GPU accelerators and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Without local storage, I/O performance is tied to network block storage throughput. However, the combination of 32 dedicated physical AMD cores and 512 GB of RAM offers strong resource density for memory-bound tasks. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data transformation pipelines, and high-density container hosting.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.32-512 is a memory-dense virtual machine instance based on AMD EPYC 9J45 x86_64 processors. Operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, the instance delivers 32 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory totals 512 GB, providing an expansive ratio of 8 GB of RAM per vCPU, which caters directly to memory-intensive computational demands. The server features no discrete GPU hardware and contains no bundled local storage, directing all primary data retention and disk I/O to network-attached block storage volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included. With its substantial memory pool and dedicated compute architecture, the configuration eliminates hypervisor oversubscription bottlenecks. This profile is engineered to support memory-heavy workloads, including distributed in-memory databases, large-scale caching solutions, complex enterprise applications, and multi-tenant container orchestration platforms.
